I'm a vet from the beginning of the game, so I have seen the changes unfold.

Depending on when you played, the problem is that hit registration is clientside. So even though you saw the hits, saw their shield flicker etc; the bullet didn't do any damage because on their client they were in a different position and didn't receive any hits.

Clearly if this is just a spike in your local traffic because Windows decided to update, that is a fair and good mechanic to have in the game. But the managers of the game have abused it to the point where sometimes I have to wonder if it is some kind of social experiment to see how much abuse people will tolerate, or how oblivious people are.

The last time I jumped into the game after an absence, I realized that the Asian players had started to not only leverage the latency in solo play, but in squad play as well. Imagine it, a whole squad of people who had, under certain conditions [like entering a room] - the ability to see you a full second before they even appeared on your screen.

Now the thing that breaks my heart about the game is how many amazing features they are adding to it - which are all meaningless because the core game is so unfair. I think they cynically think people don't get how unbalanced it is. But the pop numbers tell a different story.

The implants system has been overhauled, and they added construction. Base building & mining/harvesting mechanics for resources.

I have never understood why you would register anything PvP based on the client, it should be server side. that way it is the system that is running the game determines where the shot was and where the person was and if it hit. assuming similar ping times this puts thing in the middle, it does favor low pings over high but at least it isn't giving a different experience for the game based on ping despite being in the same match. One of the few shooters I keep going back to is Battlefield 1. I know I know, EA destroys anything they touch and they are kinda pushing the "diversity" shit in some small ways with it, but the only real difference the 'loot boxes' make gameplaywise for this one could be the melee weapons but you don't often get close enough for that to be too big a problem, otherwise the boxes are just skins and often include 1hour squad xp boosts.

If you haven't looked into it yet it's a WW1-era shooter, and the single player campaign is enjoyable but it's definitely more team-based PvP-focused, and has multiple interesting game modes with squads of up to 5 and two teams that can go up to 32 players each side for 64 total per match, and it being Battlefield the destructible environment helps mix things up quite a bit.

My personal favorite gametype is mixed-map Conquest where two teams of 32 duke it out on maps of various sizes and angles of approach to capture and hold the majority of several points on the map, each side frequently assisted with vehicles (from weapon emplacements up to tanks, planes and boats), but the game is pretty well-balanced and since each player 'class' has some form of anti-vehicle weapon the vehicles still have to play with some strategy or get destroyed quick.

I recommend trying it out at least, perhaps through a game rental service or something, but it might pique your interest.

Try foxhole. It's not an fps, and it's still in development, but it has an awesome community and great tactical layers.

It's a top down 3PS styled along the lines of WW1/WW2, but it's a fictional game and doesn't try to follow any one historical war too closely. There's two factions, the colonials and the wardens, both have identical equipment, but different models. You start out with a pistol, two clips of ammo and a hammer, any other equipment you need must be mined, built and delivered by you or someone else, so people are careful with ammunition. Also, anything bigger than an LGM requires a crew of at least two to operate, so teamwork is mandatory, lone wolves get nowhere. Larger vehicles like tanks and gunboats require three people. Tanks also need infantry support to be useful, so even a tank crew can't be lone wolves.

This should give you an idea of the flavour of the game.
